title: Performance characterization of Ni60-WC coating on steel processed with supersonic laser deposition

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: Ni alloy particles are mostly spherical with some satellite particles. WC particles are clumped together.
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Particle_Size_Other: Most nickel alloy particles are in the range of 30-50 μm. WC powder diameter is ~10 μm.

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: cross-sections of the coating specimens were polished and then etched with the chemical solution which consists of 5 g FeCl3, 2 ml HCl and 99 ml ethanol.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: A large amount of small, bright and white particles, which sizes of the range from 1 μm to 3 μm, are observed. small pits and pores are distributed in the matrix. thin and white dendritic crystals in the matrix are likely to be chromium carbide

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: the larger bright objects are distributed in the matrix with larger pits and pores. larger polygonal and bright object are WC particles, the small white crystals probably are Cr7C3 and Cr23C6, and the matrix may be with FeNi. the sizes of the  white particles and the small white crystals increase with the increase in laser power. the sizes of some WC particles are over 2 μm, and they exhibit partially dendritic crystals
